entities.summary:
Scouting is a world-wide movement for the education of youth, founded by Robert Baden-Powell in 1907. This movement revolutionized the way young people engage in community service, outdoor skills, and leadership development. By 1920, scouting had spread to over 40 countries, with millions of members. Scouting's emphasis on character development, teamwork, and problem-solving has made it a lasting influence on youth organizations globally.

Scouting's impact extends beyond its own organization, as it has inspired numerous youth programs and initiatives. In the 1950s, scouting played a significant role in the development of the Boy Scouts of America, which continues to be a leading youth organization in the United States. Scouting's emphasis on outdoor education and environmental stewardship has also influenced the development of programs like the Nature Conservancy's Scout Programs.

Today, scouting remains an important part of youth development, with millions of young people participating in scouting programs around the world. The movement continues to evolve, incorporating new technologies and innovations to better serve its members.

The scouting movement's most famous quote, 'Do your best,' encapsulates its core values: hard work, dedication, and a commitment to making a positive impact.

Scouting's influence can be seen in various aspects of modern society, from the development of youth sports leagues to the growth of environmental activism. As a global movement, scouting has played a significant role in shaping the way young people engage with their communities and develop into responsible, compassionate leaders.

Scouting's legacy is a testament to the power of grassroots organizations to drive positive change. As the movement continues to adapt to the needs of its members and the world around them, it remains a shining example of the impact that can be achieved through the power of collective effort and determination.
